summary: Vault can encrypt variables or whole files; encrypted content carries the !vault tag and | marker (plus a vault ID label if used). Encrypted variables are decrypted on demand, while encrypted files are decrypted whenever loaded or referenced.
questions: Should I encrypt individual variables or whole files with Vault?
What does the !vault tag mean in YAML?
When does Ansible decrypt vault-encrypted files?
Can I encrypt tasks files with Vault?

answer_card.title: Encrypted variables vs encrypted files
answer_card.answer_md:
| | Encrypted variables | Encrypted files |
|---|---|---|
| What's encrypted | Variables inside a plaintext file | The entire file |
| When decrypted | On demand, when needed | Whenever loaded or referenced |
| What can be encrypted | Only variables | Any structured data file |

Encrypted content always includes the `!vault` tag and a `|` (multi-line string); content made with `--vault-id` also includes the ID label. Ansible decrypts every referenced encrypted file because it can't know what it needs otherwise.
